key_big: Every number above 1 is a product of primes: 72 = 2³ × 3².
key_sub: Use a factor tree. Stop only when every branch is a prime.
body_html:
How it works

Index notation shows repeated multiplication: 2 × 2 × 2 = 23. The 2 is the base and the 3 is the exponent (or index).

Every whole number above 1 is either prime or a product of primes. Use a factor tree: split the number into two factors and keep going until every branch is prime. Then write the primes in order with exponents.

Example

Write 72 as a product of prime factors.

72 = 8 × 9 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3.

Answer: 23 × 32

Example

Work out 34.

3 × 3 × 3 × 3.

Answer: 81

Example

Use primes to find the HCF of 12 = 22 × 3 and 18 = 2 × 32.

Shared primes, lower powers: 2 × 3.

Answer: 6

Common mistakes

  • Working out 23 as 2 × 3 = 6. It is 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
  • Stopping the factor tree at 4 or 9. They are not prime.
  • Writing 1 as a prime factor. 1 is not prime.
  • Swapping the base and exponent: 2 × 2 × 2 is 23, not 32.

faq.a: A short way to write repeated multiplication. 5 × 5 × 5 = 5³, where 5 is the base and 3 is the exponent.

faq.q: How do I write a number as a product of prime factors?
faq.a: Draw a factor tree, splitting the number until every branch is prime. Then write the primes in order using exponents, for example 72 = 2³ × 3².
No. A prime number has exactly two factors. 1 has only one.

faq.q: How do prime factors help with HCF and LCM?
faq.a: For the HCF, multiply the primes both numbers share, with the lower power. For the LCM, multiply every prime, with the higher power.

items.q: The 412 bus leaves every 12 minutes and the 415 bus every 15 minutes. They start together. How long until they are together again?
items.e: This is the LCM of 12 and 15: 60 minutes.
